findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler can no longer be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler but implements none of its abstract members (counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and the newly added build_occurrence_and_event_data) and only contains `pass`. Detector.detector_handler unconditionally does `group_type.detector_handler(self)`, so any detector of type metric_alert_fire will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class ...` instead of returning the previous no-op `evaluate() -> []`. That exception propagates out of process_detectors and breaks processing for the whole data packet, not just this detector.

findings.title: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds expected occurrence for the wrong group key
findings.body: The expected occurrence is built with `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, ...)`, but evaluate_group_key_value is then called with group_key "group_key" and value 10. build_mock_occurrence_and_event derives the occurrence fingerprint from the supplied group_key via handler.build_fingerprint(), so the expected occurrence has fingerprint `<detector_id>:val1` while the occurrence actually produced inside evaluate_group_key_value has fingerprint `<detector_id>:group_key`. The DetectorEvaluationResult equality comparison therefore cannot match and this test fails / does not verify the dedupe path as intended; the helper should be called with "group_key".

findings.title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The signature of StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate was changed in this PR to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, and the implementation builds a dict, but the docstring at line 230 still says it 'returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult'. This misdocuments the new contract that callers such as process_detectors now rely on (they call .values() on the result).
